## Finding: inaccurate closeout, not an upstream repair claim
At pm-presets default commit `8d4ac9d1e0febf32b1bfb3d343d097776e96703e`, [PR #183](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-presets/pull/183) closes [pm-7km8](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-presets/blob/8d4ac9d1e0febf32b1bfb3d343d097776e96703e/.agents/pm/issues/pm-7km8.toon) as delivered by [PR #170](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-presets/pull/170), and adds its upstream-template-defect title under [Unreleased / Fixed](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-presets/blob/8d4ac9d1e0febf32b1bfb3d343d097776e96703e/CHANGELOG.md).

The same canonical item distinguishes the package's fail-closed compatibility mitigation from the upstream parser/flag-extractor fix, explicitly says the upstream follow-up stays open, and requires host SDK/CLI own-key regression coverage before revisiting those refusals. PR #170's merge and timestamp are real; they do not establish that the host defect was repaired.

## Current source evidence and bounded reproduction
Reviewed host source at `unbraind/pm-cli@1a72d089ddf83d7347c40431bb0bd2e769f3c43d`:
- [templates.ts](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/1a72d089ddf83d7347c40431bb0bd2e769f3c43d/src/sdk/templates.ts): `parseStoredTemplateOptions` initializes `normalized = {}` and assigns arbitrary accepted keys using indexed assignment; `builtinTemplateDocument` directly indexes `BUILTIN_TEMPLATES[normalizedName]` without an own-property check.
- [type-synonyms.ts](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/1a72d089ddf83d7347c40431bb0bd2e769f3c43d/src/core/item/type-synonyms.ts): `resolveTypeSynonym` directly indexes the ordinary-object table.

A Node v24.22.1 isolated probe using extracted exact pure functions (not the full SDK/CLI) passed six assertions:
1. Input `JSON.parse('{"__proto__":"public-data","ordinary":"kept","constructor":"kept"}')` owns `__proto__`.
2. `parseStoredTemplateOptions(input,"own-key")` does not own that key.
3–4. Ordinary and constructor string controls remain.
5. `builtinTemplateDocument("constructor")` returns a document with that name despite no own builtin entry.
6. `typeof resolveTypeSynonym("constructor") === "function"`, rather than the documented string-or-undefined result.

These are source-qualified helper reproductions supporting the status discrepancy, not an end-to-end installed release test, exploit claim, or evidence of live impact. No provider operations were performed. No source/runtime/dependency files changed in #183.

## Expected / actual / impact
Expected: close and attribute the delivered adapter mitigation accurately while retaining an explicit unresolved upstream follow-up unless separate upstream repair evidence exists.
Actual: the unresolved host defect itself is marked closed and appears as Fixed, even though the canonical record and current source still distinguish it from the delivered mitigation.
Impact: generated release notes and agent work selection can incorrectly treat host fidelity work as completed. This is not a new regression in the adapter's fail-closed protection and does not imply any npm publication.

## Acceptance criteria
- Correct the pm-7km8 status/resolution and generated changelog, or split the completed adapter mitigation from the still-open upstream follow-up with verified links.
- If closure is intended, supply the actual upstream repair revision and relevant SDK/CLI regression evidence; do not cite an adapter-only merge as the host fix.
- Preserve existing tracker/history evidence; append a corrective event rather than rewriting old history.
- Add a focused closeout/regression check that a mitigation-only merge cannot attribute an explicitly unresolved upstream defect as Fixed.
- Keep the adapter's compatibility refusals until the documented host support criteria are met.

Deduplication: reviewed all 183 all-status pm-presets issues/PRs and the canonical item, plus PR #183 conversation; no separate existing corrective issue found.
Closeout marks unresolved upstream template SDK defect as fixed by adapter mitigation
